title: Route proxy retired (opencode#1153) while deployed config + live sessions still route through opencode-route/:18750 — retirement gate missing

body:
## What happened

Commit e8b4cdc75 ("rewire OpenClaw to the server facade and retire the route proxy (opencode#1153)", landed 2026-11-04 10:57 CST) deleted `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` + `bin/opencode-route-proxy-start.sh` and removed the `opencode-route-proxy.service` definition from `home/common/default.nix`. The unit was stopped at 10:54 CST and the files were removed from the live deploy dir (`~/code/bin`).

But the deployed OpenCode config still routes through that proxy: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (and the repo's `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`) still carry 52 `opencode-route` references, and every dispatched session runs model `opencode-route/workhorse` against `127.0.0.1:18750`. The opencode#1146 server-façade cutover that was supposed to make the standalone proxy unnecessary has NOT landed in the deployed config.

## Impact

- Every `opencode-route/*` session failed from 10:54 CST onward (surfaced as provider.auth 401s).
- The #3232 receipt-validation audit session burned all 3 of its monitor resume attempts against the dead route and was marked failed-final, even though all four of its gates had closed and the audit itself is still owed (issue closed via PR #5576; the audit deliverable is outstanding).
- Any other workhorse-tier work dispatched in that window hit the same wall.

## Stopgap applied (2026-11-04 ~12:03 CST, laptop only, no repo change)

- Restored `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`, `bin/opencode-route-proxy-start.sh`, and the test file into `~/code/bin` from `e8b4cdc75^` (md5-verified byte-identical; untracked files in that checkout).
- Installed a hand-placed user unit `~/.config/systemd/user/opencode-route-proxy.service` replicating the retired nix unit (port 18750, Restart=always), enabled and started it.
- Verified: unit active, listening on 18750, `/health` ok, `/v1/models` serves the tier list, and a live `scout` completion returned HTTP 200 end-to-end. (Workhorse/specialist currently return honest quota 429/502s — the Go Flash carriers are in a trough until popesdrew's 5h reset at 18:47Z; drewrypope weekly is walled until Nov 9. That part is quota, not plumbing.)
- The #3232 session has been resumed with full context.

## What's owed

1. **A retirement gate**: never retire a provider door (files, unit, or port) while the deployed config still references it. The retirement check must grep the deployed `opencode.jsonc` (and the session dispatch state) for the provider id before removing anything.
2. **A durable home for the proxy until the cutover actually lands**: either restore the files + unit in the repo/home config until opencode#1154's cutover changes the deployed config, or formally adopt the hand-placed user unit as the interim mechanism and record it. The stopgap above is deliberately out-of-band and should not silently become permanent.
3. **Remove the stopgap when the façade cutover lands** in the deployed config (opencode-route references gone from the deployed jsonc), and close this issue with that evidence.

Related: opencode#1146 (façade program), opencode#1153 (the retirement), opencode#1154 (cutover), code#5295 (known-exhausted gate), code#3232 (the audit that was blocked).

## Acceptance criteria

- A retirement gate exists: removing a route/proxy component fails or blocks while deployed config or live session routing still references it (checked against the `opencode-route` reference counts in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc` and the repo `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`).
- For the opencode-route retirement specifically, the end state is one of: deployed config migrated to the server façade (the opencode#1146 cutover), or the proxy remains deployed as a repo-managed unit — the hand-placed stopgap unit is not the final state.
- The outstanding #3232 receipt-validation audit deliverable (its monitor attempts were burned against the dead route) is re-run or explicitly re-filed.
